html:
The Kuruaya are an Indigenous people of the lower Xingu River region in the Brazilian state of Pará, living on its tributaries such as the Curuá River. Their language, close to that of the Munduruku, belongs to the Tupian family and is no longer spoken in daily life.

In the 1900s rubber tappers of the rubber boom moved into their lands, and many Kuruaya were drawn into rubber work and mixed with settlers in the town of Altamira. Today about 150 live in their own Indigenous area. Their neighbours on the Xingu were the Yudjá.
